# =============================================================================
# PiSonic — first-boot configuration
# =============================================================================
#
# HOW TO USE
#   1. Flash the prebuilt image to the SD card.
#   2. On any computer, open the SD card's small FAT ("boot") partition.
#   3. Edit this pisonic-config.txt with a plain-text editor, then save.
#   4. Insert the card into the Pi 3A+ and power it on.
#
# The radio reads /pisonic-config.txt before WiFi / hostname / SSH / time are
# brought up and applies each active setting once. Each key=value line is
# commented only after that setting is successfully stored on the persistent
# data partition. A failed or invalid setting stays active and is retried on the
# next boot. To apply a stored setting again, edit its value, remove the leading
# #, and reboot.
#
# FORMAT
#   * One  key=value  per line.
#   * Lines starting with #, and blank lines, are ignored.
#   * Remove the leading "#" to activate a setting.
#   * Values may optionally be wrapped in "double" or 'single' quotes.
#
# A bad or missing file never blocks boot — the image's built-in defaults are
# used instead. See /tmp/provision-from-boot.log on the device for what was
# applied or skipped. Uncomment and replace the placeholders below before first
# boot. Placeholder/example values are rejected rather than installed.
# =============================================================================

# --- WiFi (REQUIRED: the Pi 3A+ has no Ethernet) -----------------------------
# Only WPA-PSK (WPA2 personal) networks are supported.
# The passphrase must be 8..63 characters.
# wifi_ssid=<your-wifi-name>
# wifi_psk=<your-wifi-password>

# WiFi regulatory domain: an ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. DE, US, GB).
# Applied at boot via `iw reg set` so the radio uses the channels and transmit
# power allowed where you are. Setting this also clears the "reason -52" channel
# errors seen in dmesg under the default worldwide domain. Leave it commented to
# keep the safe worldwide default ("00").
# wifi_country=DE

# --- Static IP (OPTIONAL — leave commented for automatic DHCP) ----------------
# By default the radio requests its address automatically over DHCP. To pin a
# fixed address instead, uncomment ip_address (a dotted-quad IPv4) and, usually,
# ip_gateway. ip_prefix is the CIDR mask length (1..32; 24 = a normal /24 home
# network) and defaults to 24 if omitted. ip_dns is an optional space-separated
# list of up to three DNS servers. A malformed value falls back to DHCP.
# ip_address=192.168.1.42
# ip_prefix=24
# ip_gateway=192.168.1.1
# ip_dns=192.168.1.1 1.1.1.1

# --- Identity ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The hostname is also the AirPlay / Spotify Connect device name.
# Letters, digits and hyphens only.
# hostname=pisonic

# --- Access / debugging ------------------------------------------------------
# Root password login is locked in the generic image. To use console or SSH
# login, choose a unique password here; known placeholders such as "changeme"
# are rejected. SSH cannot be enabled until this password is safely persisted.
# root_password=<choose-a-unique-password>

# Enable (1) or disable (0) the SSH server (dropbear). Default: disabled.
enable_ssh=0

# --- Locale / time -----------------------------------------------------------
# Time zone, e.g. Europe/London. Applied only if the zoneinfo database is
# present in the image; otherwise ignored (UTC is used). Without this the
# top status-bar clock on the display shows UTC. Change it to your own zone
# (any name under /usr/share/zoneinfo, e.g. Europe/London, America/New_York).
timezone=UTC

# Use a specific NTP server instead of the default public pool. Handy on
# locked-down networks that only allow a local time source.
# ntp_server=pool.ntp.org

# --- NOTE ON THE SOUND CARD --------------------------------------------------
# The generic image initially uses the built-in headphone output. After WiFi is
# working, use the web interface's Audio page to select an I2S DAC/amp; it keeps
# config.txt and all userspace audio settings in sync, then asks you to reboot.
